universal-ctags 6.2.1's Terraform parser tags every key = value pair inside a nested object/list literal within a locals block's own attribute value as its own separate 'local' definition (verified directly: examples/network-acls/main.tf's locals.network_acls = {...} nested rule maps alone produce 16 spurious 'cidr_block' local tags at one nesting depth) -- of ctags' 739 combined 'local' tags across both subjects, 100% of the unmatched ones (225 on terraform-aws-vpc alone) are this false-positive class; every real resource/data/module/variable/output ctags tag matched a fathom definition (0 misses). 'local' is therefore excluded from both sides' kind intersection (like 'provider') rather than trusted as ground truth.
disposition: deferred: L1 is excellent (sym_recall 1.0, sym_precision .9864) once universal-ctags' 'local' kind is excluded from the kind intersection as unreliable ground truth (see notes) -- the terraform queue item's L3 target is out of reach this pass. L2 (tool-format 'reference recall/precision', design table 1.2) and L3 (import_resolution / file_edge_precision/recall) both need an oracle at tier A or C (design table 1.3); this item's named oracle is 'terraform graph (tier A, offline init)', which needs `terraform init` to resolve every subject's declared providers. Measured directly against the registry before attempting it: the AWS provider alone (both subjects use it; eks additionally needs kubernetes/helm/tls/cloudinit/null/local/time) ships a 127 MiB compressed darwin/arm64 zip (registry.terraform.io metadata, 2026-09-28) -- an uncompressed Go provider binary of that class typically lands 2-3x larger, and combined with the terraform CLI itself (26 MiB compressed) and eks's extra providers this exceeds the language-breadth run's stated 300 MiB per-worker disk ceiling well before a single `terraform graph` runs, even held only transiently. No tier-C oracle is available either: an independent second implementation of HCL reference extraction would need to be written and would not be genuinely independent of this dialect's own hashicorp/hcl/v2-based extractor without real, separate authorship -- self-grading the extractor's own Calls output with a same-library second pass is exactly the kind of ungrounded measurement design §14.2 rules out. The Calls edges (design §1.1 L2 'resource reference edges': resource/data/module/output intra-file references, locals per-attribute, depends_on) and module source recording (local-path and registry refs, in Signature) are implemented and unit-tested (internal/extractor/hclextract_test.go) but genuinely unmeasured -- 'not-attempted', not claimed. LB-Q-terraform stays unchecked; see LB-Q-terraform-rest. Trigger: a shared, pre-populated offline provider mirror (built once, reused across every terraform-dependent queue item rather than downloaded per item) makes tier A tractable within the disk budget, or an Opus-reviewed decision accepts a tier-C independent HCL reference parser (a second, separately-authored implementation, not this dialect's own extractor run twice) for L2/L3.
